askHelp: Starts a real human approval when a decision needs one; the review itself always uses the same shared matrix, and the mode decides only whether a question is asked.
noAskHelp: The review uses the same shared matrix; a call that needs a human decision asks nobody and does not run, settling as fallback-deny. The agent can still ask through ask or chat.
title: Enablement and approval modes
description: Approval modes only control whether the plugin starts a human approval; they do not stop the agent from using ask or chat.
boundaryGuardedHelp: After approval the call is still bound by the host workspace file sandbox; a write outside it fails, and the agent may request escalation separately through the host, which the plugin never approves for it.
boundaryTrustedHelp: After approval no workspace file sandbox is applied; other host guards still apply as usual. Changing the execution boundary does not disable the current session.
enabledHelp: When disabled, the plugin stays running in the background to record audits, but all commands are directly admitted without gate interception
subagentFixedHelp: Fixed to auto approval (no-ask) and not selectable: the host pins a delegated child session's approval policy to never, and the plugin does not open a human approval on a subtask's behalf.
subagentNote: Every subtask uses the subtask approval mode; there is no per-subtask mode switch.
sessionNote: Approval modes and the execution boundary describe plugin configuration only; whether to take over a session is always decided by that session's permission menu, and changing configuration does not enable any session.
invalidConfig: The configuration file is invalid; the last valid configuration is still in use: {error}
autoPresetError: auto preset registration failed (another auto review provider may already exist): {error}
sessionRecordError:
Writing session verdict records failed (the current permission outcome is unaffected):
{records}
historyDescription: Content snapshots are deduplicated by content; each successful apply adds one entry.
coverageDescription: Intercepting an entry point does not mean every effect inside a tool implementation is observed.
